title: Microledger: token cost & latency mapping explorations
content:
Summary:
This working doc collects early UX explorations for a token-level microledger view: a dashboard that lets engineers and product owners explore cost and latency attribution at sub-request granularity. The goal is a single-pane exploratory surface that supports fast root-cause for anomalies (spikes in per-token cost or latency) and interaction patterns for drilling into sample requests, prefixes, and cache impact.

Why a separate microledger view?
- Existing token/route dashboards show averages and percentiles; they hide distributional behavior across requests and TTL/KV cache hits.
- Micro-level visibility helps: 1) diagnose quality vs cost regressions, 2) validate batching/quantization tradeoffs on real traffic, 3) provide per-customer/per-route bill analysis for enterprise accounts.

Primary users and jobs-to-be-done:
- Platform engineer: identify which model/route increases tail latency after a rollout.
- Prod ML engineer: measure token-cost increase after moving to int8 quantization for a particular prompt family.
- Customer Success/Finance: reconcile per-route token spend with observed customer billing anomalies.

Design goals (high level):
1) Multi-scale: from aggregated heatmaps down to individual token trace.
2) Low friction: keyboard-first filtering + quick sample playback.
3) Causal hints: show likely contributors (KV cache miss rows, batching size peaks, system interrupts).
4) Defensive defaults: privacy filters for PII, redact by default for non-admins.

Wireframe variants (sketch descriptions):
Variant A — Timeline Mosaic (preferred for investigations)
- Top: Time-range selector + quick buckets (last 5m, 1h, 24h, custom).
- Middle-left: Heatmap 'microledger' grid (rows=routes or customer ids, cols=time buckets). Cell color = median per-token-cost; opacity = request volume. Hover => inline sparkline + summary (avg latency, p50/p95 cost, KV cache hit %).
- Middle-right: Sample panel (when cell clicked) shows top 10 representative requests with small event stream; each sample has a token-level mini-trace timeline (per-token latency, generation token type: prompt/assist/response) and a cost ribbon.
- Bottom: Attribution bar: stacked bars for CPU/GPU time, KV-cache delta, batching overhead. Each segment clickable to highlight affected samples.
Interaction notes:
- Hovering a cell flicks the sample panel to 'focus mode' with keyboard shortcuts (j/k to move between samples).
- 'Pin sample' makes it persist across cell changes for cross-time comparison.
- Merge/split view for comparing two time ranges side-by-side.

Variant B — Slab List + Detail Drawer (compact / admin-friendly)
- Left: sortable list of routes (+ search). Columns: total tokens, tokens/request, avg token-cost, p95 latency, cache-hit %.
- Right: detail drawer opens when a row clicked. Drawer has a waterfall chart (per-request timeline) and a per-token histogram.
- Useful for people who start with a suspect route and want a top-down view.

Variant C — Flow Mode (for onboarding / exec)
- High-level funnel: requests -> batches -> tokens -> outputs. Each stage shows median cost + failure rate. Simplified for non-technical stakeholders.

Data model & aggregation decisions: (tradeoffs to confirm with infra)
- Microtoken vs token: we define 'microtoken' as token-level events including 1) prompt tokens, 2) model-generated tokens, 3) KV-cache lookup events (when applicable).
- Storage: raw micro-events stored as sampled traces (1% uniform sampling default). Heavyweight traces captured on anomalies (p95 token-cost delta > X).
- Aggregates: precompute per-route/time-bucket aggregates (median, p50/p95/p99, volume) at 1m/5m/1h resolutions. Keep raw traces for last 7d, aggregates for 90d.
- Attribution heuristics: cache-impact = difference in median latency between cache-hit and cache-miss samples for identical route/prompt-hash. Flag samples with identical prompt-hash but differing cache-hit.

Metric mapping (UI label -> backend metric name / notes):
- Per-token-cost -> metrics.token_cost_usd_per_token (derived from per-device compute time * cost rate)
- Token-latency-ms -> metrics.token_latency_ms (includes kernel time + scheduler delays)
- KV-cache-hit -> traces.kv_cache_hit bool (nullable)
- Batch-size -> request.batch_size int
- Prompt-hash -> traces.prompt_fingerprint string (used for grouping)

Privacy & access controls:
- Defaults: redact prompt text in UI for non-CS/admin roles. Display prompt-hash and token counts. Provide 'request-inspector' permission to unredact with audit log.
- PII detection pipeline: run lightweight regex + LLM PII detector on sampled traces; add a red flag UI state.

Prototyping notes (Figma / data hookup):
- Use prototype frames 'A-mosaic' and 'B-slab' in figma link above. Build interactive hover + pin states.
- Backend endpoint: /v1/console/microledger?range=...&group_by=route,customer&bucket=1m -> returns aggregates + representative sample ids. Representative sample selection logic: highest-deviation sample and median sample per bucket.
- Sample playback: small client-side viz that replays token timings to show spikes; consider SVG-based rendering with request scrubber.

Backlog grooming (epic breakdown, tentative estimates):
- INF-2101: microledger backend aggregates (compute + storage) — 8 SP — owner: Samir
- INF-2102: sample trace storage + sampling policy — 5 SP — owner: Arjun
- INF-2103: Figma high-fidelity Mosaic prototype + design token set — 3 SP — owner: Lena
- INF-2104: Console frontend mosaic + sample panel (basic) — 13 SP — owner: Maya
- INF-2105: Access controls + redaction UI — 5 SP — owner: Priya
- INF-2106: Playback micro-trace viz + keyboard navigation — 8 SP — owner: Maya
- INF-2107: Alerts/Auto-summaries (auto-detect regressions & open toast) — 5 SP — owner: Product/Eng pairing

Grooming notes:
- Priority: start with INF-2101, INF-2103, INF-2104 in a 6-week sprint to unblock prototype demos for QBR.
- Early MVP scope: 1m/5m aggregates, single-customer grouping, sample panel with token-level sparkline, pinned comparison across two buckets.

Open questions / risks:
1) Cost of storing and querying microtraces at high QPS. Mitigation: aggressive sampling + anomaly-triggered capture.
2) Backend latency for on-demand sample hydration. Need to timebox 95th percentile SLA for UI (<500ms on interactive queries).
3) Accuracy of attribution heuristics (cache impact vs model change) — requires labeled rollout experiments to validate.
4) Security: exposing prompt text to CS team. Need clear RBAC and audit trails before unredacting.

Experiment ideas (for validation):
- A/B rollout: enable microledger for 10 customers and measure time-to-resolution on incident playbacks.
- Cache-needle test: force cache miss for a controlled subset and verify attribution metric flags cache impact.

Next steps (action items):
- Design: Lena to produce 2 high-fidelity screens for Mosaic and Slab by 2024-06-28.
- Backend: Samir/Arjun to prototype a 1m-bucket aggregator on staging with synthetic data by 2024-07-05.
- Product: Maya to prepare demo script and 3 example incident scenarios for QBR review.

Notes to self / loose thoughts (informal):
- Consider a compact micro-ledger export CSV for finance teams (route, time range, tokens, cost breakdown).
- Might be useful to surface 'cost per generated token' vs 'cost per request' side-by-side — helps ML teams decide output-length tradeoffs.
- Think about mobile-friendly condensed view for on-call.

References / inspiration:
- Internal: per-request token inspector draft (see linked PR).
- External inspiration: "chronicle"-style time series investigation tools, and observability UIs that combine heatmap + sample trace (New Relic, Datadog session traces).

If you're reviewing: please add inline comments in Figma frames and add notes to INF-2101 if you have infra objections.
